## 1. a001: I missed pruning a few dead branches in an apple tree. Can I remove them in the summer?

Source: https://apples.extension.org/i-missed-pruning-a-few-dead-branches-in-an-apple-tree-can-i-remove-them-in-the-summer/

**Coverage_q = 3 / 3 = 100.0%** (COVERED 1, INFERABLE 2, ABSENT 0)

### p1 · COVERED

**Atomic fact:** The best time to prune an apple tree is early in the spring before bud break.

- Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes
- Judge reasoning: The linked source directly states the proposition, including its load-bearing conditions and assertion strength.
- Portal route:
  - https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/tree_lifecycle?env=orchard&op=ODG00
  - https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/tree_lifecycle?env=orchard&stage=OAR70&op=OAR70
- Authoritative source:
  - extension oregonstate edu catalog pnw 400 training pruning your home orchard <https://extension.oregonstate.edu/catalog/pnw-400-training-pruning-your-home-orchard>
  - Pruning and training apple trees <https://extension.umn.edu/garden-and-home/yard-and-garden/gardening-in-minnesota/pruning-and-training-apple-trees> (General pruning guidelines; Pruning to restore or renovate an old tree)
- Evidence:
  - > Prune when all danger from fall or early winter freeze has passed but before growth begins in spring. Sweet cherry trees may be pruned in August when there’s less risk of bacterial infection.
  - > Fruit trees should be pruned every year in late winter or early spring, preferably after the coldest weather has passed and before growth begins. Prune minimally, especially with young trees, as excessive pruning will delay or reduce fruiting and create too much leafy growth.
- Searches:
  - prun* AND (spring OR dormant) → 751 chunks; full results in a001_searches.json
  - "dead branches" OR "broken branches" → 28 chunks; full results in a001_searches.json
  - "summer pruning" AND (limit OR minimal OR light) → 141 chunks; full results in a001_searches.json

### p2 · INFERABLE

**Atomic fact:** Dead or broken branches can be removed from an apple tree at any time of year (including summer).

- Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes
- Judge reasoning: CSU (fruit trees): broken branches should be removed immediately, i.e. whenever they occur, not held for the dormant season; UMaine: dead branches can be eliminated without further thought. Step: dead or broken branches can be removed at any time of year, including summer. BORDERLINE: 'immediately' is stated for broken branches; for dead wood the any-season timing is the inference. Both live 200.
- Portal route:
  - https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/tree_lifecycle?env=orchard&stage=ODG02&op=OAR70
- Portal card:
  - Pruning & Training > Summer pruning
- Authoritative source:
  - 1210 – Pruning Mature Fruit Trees – PlantTalk Colorado <https://planttalk.colostate.edu/?p=1043> (CSU PlantTalk 1210 Pruning Mature Fruit Trees)
  - Pruning - Cooperative Extension: Tree Fruits - University of Maine Cooperative Extension <https://extension.umaine.edu/fruit/growing-fruit-trees-in-maine/pruning/> (UMaine Extension, Pruning (fruit trees))
- Evidence:
  - > Broken branches should be removed immediately. When removing dead branches, sterilize tools between cuttings in case the branches were killed by disease. Alcohol or a bleach solution can be used as a disinfectant. When removing diseased branches, make the pruning cut about six inches below the diseased area. Again, be sure to disinfect the pruners between each cut.
  - > Dead branches are not essential to the tree and can be eliminated without further thought. They are typically removed with thinning cuts when the entire branch has died. If only the tip is dead, it can be removed with a heading cut by pruning at a point just above a side branch when it is not desired to remove the entire branch.
- Searches:

  - "dead branches" OR "broken branches" → 28 chunks; full results in a001_searches.json
  - "summer pruning" AND (limit OR minimal OR light) → 141 chunks; full results in a001_searches.json

Tropical-orchard paper is not apple evidence. Year-round premise remains unsupported.

### p3 · INFERABLE

**Atomic fact:** Outside the early-spring pruning window (e.g. when removing dead branches in summer), other pruning should be kept to a minimum.

- Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes
- Judge reasoning: UMN explicitly recommends minimal pruning, especially (not exclusively) on young trees, and explains fruiting and vegetative-growth penalties. This general restriction applies to nonessential live-wood cuts during summer too; the normal annual-pruning window is separately stated. No inference of year-round permission to remove dead wood is made.

  - > The lack of true-from-seed production is even more extreme in fruit crops. ## 39. a044: How are finished apple trees produced in a nursery?

Source: https://apples.extension.org/how-are-finished-apple-trees-produced-in-a-nursery/

**Coverage_q = 31 / 31 = 100.0%** (COVERED 29, INFERABLE 2, ABSENT 0)

### p1 · COVERED

**Atomic fact:** In the nursery production schedule for fruit trees, rootstock liners are cut/dug in late fall.

- Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes
- Judge reasoning: Linked source explicitly supports the proposition; quantities, timing and modality retained.
- Portal route:
  - https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/tree_lifecycle?env=orchard&stage=ODG00&op=ODG00
- Portal card:
  - Modify Landscape > Tree Nursery and Grade Selection
- Authoritative source:
  - Penn State Tree Fruit Production Guide <https://extension.psu.edu/tree-fruit-production-guide> (page 7)
- Evidence:
  - > The traditional tree is produced in a three-year cycle. Fall of year one daughter rootstock liners are cut from the mother stool beds and graded based on diameter, freedom from spines, and general straightness of the stem. The preferred diameter is $ \frac{3}{16} $ to $ \frac{7}{16} $ inch in diameter. They are kept in cold storage for the winter. Rootstock liners are planted the following spring

### p1 · COVERED

## 47. a053: Do trees planted on dwarfing rootstocks produce small apples?

Source: https://apples.extension.org/do-trees-planted-on-dwarfing-rootstocks-produce-small-apples/

**Coverage_q = 3 / 3 = 100.0%** (COVERED 0, INFERABLE 3, ABSENT 0)

### p1 · INFERABLE

**Atomic fact:** A dwarfing rootstock can reduce vegetative growth, resulting in a tree with a smaller trunk, shorter height, narrower canopy and lower root volume.

- Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes
- Judge reasoning: CABI: dwarfing rootstocks reduce scion vigour so trees grow as dwarf, closely planted trees, by slowing and ending shoot extension earlier (smaller height and canopy, hence trunk). IPDM p.31: dwarfing rootstocks such as M9, O3 and M26 have smaller, finer root systems. Kept as INFERABLE.
- Portal route:
  - https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/tree_lifecycle?env=orchard&stage=ODG00&op=ODG00

  - Apples: Botany, Production and Uses <https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/api/kb/assets/pdf/435dfba709ef04c7/Apples%20-%20Botany%2C%20Production%20and%20Uses%20-%20D.%20Ferree%2C%20I.%20Warrington%20%28CABI%2C%202003%29%20BBS.pdf> (page 96)

- Evidence:
  - > Choice of the appropriate rootstock and/or interstock can enable the fruit grower to control the inherent vigour of the scion tree, so making possible and facilitating the adoption of a chosen system of tree spacing, pruning and training (Ferree and Carlson, 1987; Wertheim, 1998). Many apple rootstocks/interstocks reduce the strong vigour of scions, allowing them to be grown as dwarf, closely plan
  - > It is important to note that the dwarfing influence of rootstocks on apple scions is different from that achieved when using most compact scion cultivars or chemical plant-growth regulators. - Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes
- Judge reasoning: CABI: T-budding needs slipping bark (late July–early September in the northern hemisphere) while chip budding does not; UGA: warm-climate June budding versus dormant budding. Timing depends on location and technique.
- Portal route:
  - https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/tree_lifecycle?env=orchard&stage=ODG00&op=ODG00
- Portal card:
  - Pruning & Training > Bud grafting
  - Pruning & Training > Budding season
- Authoritative source:
  - Apples: Botany, Production and Uses <https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/api/kb/assets/pdf/435dfba709ef04c7/Apples%20-%20Botany%2C%20Production%20and%20Uses%20-%20D.%20Ferree%2C%20I.%20Warrington%20%28CABI%2C%202003%29%20BBS.pdf> (page 141)
  - Apples: Botany, Production and Uses <https://applelifecycle-3094d65c1fea.herokuapp.com/api/kb/assets/pdf/435dfba709ef04c7/Apples%20-%20Botany%2C%20Production%20and%20Uses%20-%20D.%20Ferree%2C%20I.%20Warrington%20%28CABI%2C%202003%29%20BBS.pdf> (page 142)
  - University of Georgia Extension Bulletin 818 — Propagating Deciduous Fruit Plants Common to Georgia <https://fieldreport.caes.uga.edu/publications/B818/propagating-deciduous-fruit-plants-common-to-georgia/> (T-budding (June budding; dormant budding) — reviewed February 2026)
- Evidence:
  - > Two techniques of budding, T- and chip budding, are used for propagation of apple trees. In both techniques it is essential to achieve effective joining of the cambial layers of the scion bud and the rootstock and to prevent desiccation. In T-budding, a T-shaped incision is made in the rootstock rind at the time in summer when the bark easily slips from the underlying xylem to facilitate bud inser
  - > In chip budding, an oval shield with the central scion bud replaces an exactly similarly shaped piece of bark removed from the rootstock and consequently the cambia of the two partners usually match very well (Plate 6.13). Both chips are cut out in a similar manner. On the bud stick, the first cut is made 0.5 cm below the bud down into the wood at an angle of $ 30-45^{\circ} $ to a depth of approx
  - > This method of propagation is used in the summer (called June budding) or late summer (called dormant budding). Apple and pear trees 3 years old or less may be topworked by T-budding if a variety change is desired. June budding is done as soon as mature current season's buds can be cut (mid-June) and continues through July. Two to three weeks after budding, cut the rootstocks off about a half inch
- Searches:
  - budding season by latitude/climate, June budding, dormant chip budding, budwood handling → Read CABI §6.6 (printed 141–142), Penn State bud-grafting video, UGA B818 (reviewed Feb 2026, live 200), Wisconsin budding article, UNH grafting. No source for March dormant chip budding.

Source: https://apples.extension.org/how-can-i-control-insects-and-diseases-on-my-apple-tree/

### p1 · INFERABLE

**Atomic fact:** Pests can do a surprising amount of damage to apples grown by homeowners.

- Denominator: yes (counted: apple / apple-orchard information)
- Numerator: yes

Adequate control of these pests usually requires sprays containing fungicides and insecticides 10 to 15 times throughout
